reasons_for_inclusion: Carefully argued and heavily referenced; built on original interviews with PKD's ex-wives and a primary-source check of Britannica editions.
Directly load-bearing for the Works entry on Ubik and for the precognition strand of PKD reception.
A useful, well-documented example of the parapsychological reading of Dick — valuable precisely as a position to represent and weigh, not endorse.
reasons_for_exclusion: Advances an unfalsifiable precognition thesis in an advocacy venue; must be framed as a contested claim, never as settled fact.
editorial_angle: Publish (not feature) as a 'serious but contested' reception piece. Lead with the article's strongest, lane-independent move — the negative case that Dick couldn't have known of ubiquinone — then present the precognition inference as the author's own carefully hedged conclusion.
curator_notes: This is the canonical 'distinguish serious scholarship from pop-occult/spam' case the curation criteria describe: it is unambiguously NOT spam (rigorous, sourced, candid), yet its thesis is fringe and unprovable. content_class=serious_scholarship with scholarly_value=medium and a mandatory contested-claim frame captures that nuance. Note: the article's acknowledgments thank portal-affiliated scholars including Ted Hand.
